video-vegan-recipes-goodful-aoz9c5lfvk-y.title: Three Vegan Grilled Cheese Builds: 5 Minutes, 50 Minutes, and 5 Hours
video-vegan-recipes-goodful-aoz9c5lfvk-y.summary: Goodful’s video presents a side‑by‑side exploration of vegan grilled cheese at three different time commitments. Host Merle guides viewers through a rapid 5‑minute tofu‑based cheese, a 50‑minute cashew‑based cheese with agar agar and tapioca for melt, and a full 5‑hour production that includes homemade bread, roasted-tomato soup, and two vegan cheeses (smoked gouda and cheddar). The episode emphasizes sustainability (cloth-wrapped tofu pressing), plant-based flavor boosters (nutritional yeast, miso, lemon juice, herbs), and meltability achieved with vegan thickeners (agar agar, tapioca starch, kappa carrageenan). It also features practical kitchen techniques (toasting bread, using a Dutch oven, immersion blender for soup) and a simple side salad to accompany the final sandwich. The video blends quick execution with a from-scratch offer, ending with tasting notes and encouragement to try the homemade approach.

video-vegan-recipes-goodful-fjllt3ywc4-y.title: Make It Vegan Marathon: LA Vegan Cookies, Burgers, Mac and Cheese, and Sushi
video-vegan-recipes-goodful-fjllt3ywc4-y.summary: In this Goodful Make It Vegan Marathon episode, host Merle enlists her friend Arya to hunt for the best vegan chocolate chip cookies in the LA area, then returns to the kitchen to recreate and veganize a chocolate chip cookie together. The show expands into a broader plant-based tasting and cooking spree, including a burger segment (featuring a Monty's-style vegan burger and a homemade vegan patty using tofu, mushrooms, beets, and vital wheat gluten), a cashew-based mac and cheese, and a vegan sushi project that mimics tuna and eel using tomatoes and eggplant. Interludes include live trivia and taste tests with quick verdicts (e.g., the Merlio cookie is ranked a perfect 10 by Merle, while Erin McKenna’s cookie scores around 7.75). Across segments, the episode showcases practical vegan substitutions (coconut oil instead of butter, fruit purees and arrowroot instead of eggs, non-dairy milks, vegan cheese substitutes) and a playful emphasis on approachable, DIY vegan meals that aim to satisfy non-vegan appetites and encourage experimentation at home.

video-vegan-recipes-goodful-khl2digi14-y.title: Vegan Drumsticks from Yuba (Tofu Skin) — Rehydration, Wrapping, and Air Fryer Finish
video-vegan-recipes-goodful-khl2digi14-y.summary: In this Goodful video, Merle attempts to craft vegan drumsticks using yuba (tofu skin). The process covers slicing frozen yuba, rehydrating it in water, wringing out excess moisture, and seasoning with a bouillon-based mix plus five-spice. Strips are wrapped around a core with a cornstarch slurry to resemble drumsticks, chilled briefly, and then glazed and finished in an air fryer at 325°F (160°C). The result is four formed pieces with a notable skin-like texture and color, which Merle rates highly and suggests as a crowd-pleasing vegan option. The video also references fellow creator Woon Hang for recipe inspiration.

video-vegan-recipes-goodful-0vgf96o1gug-.title: 2-Minute vs 2-Day Vegan Chocolate Chip Cookies
video-vegan-recipes-goodful-0vgf96o1gug-.summary: In this Goodful video, Merle presents two vegan chocolate chip cookie approaches side by side: a fast 2-minute version baked in the microwave and a 2-day, flavor-deepened version that builds toffee, crushed chocolate, and an oats-brown-butter dough, chilled for 48 hours before baking. The quick method relies on refined coconut oil, light brown sugar, vanilla, and applesauce to form a dough that comes together with flour and chips before microwaving on a prepared plate. The 2-day method introduces a separate toffee element (vegan butter, brown sugar, salt, cooked to 290°F/143°C), oats hydrated with boiling water, browned Miyoko’s butter emulsified with ice and water, and a sugar-bath dough enriched with espresso powder, vanilla, and flour. The dough is folded with crushed toffee and chocolate, chilled for 48 hours, portioned into balls, baked at 325°F (160°C) for 18–20 minutes, and finished with a cohesive balance of sweetness, salt, toffee crunch, and chocolate. The video highlights ingredient choices, texture and flavor development, and timing strategies—showing that patience yields a noticeably richer vegan cookie.

She offers practical notes and uses for each category, such as soaking dried chickpeas for hummus and falafel, lentils as a protein source, oat milk from oats, jackfruit as a canned meat substitute, and coconut milk for cooking or dairy-free creams. The tour also covers flavor builders (soy sauce, vegan mayo, vinegars, sauces), nut-based cheese options (cashews, tahini, nutritional yeast), and egg-replacement techniques (flax eggs, black salt with turmeric for tofu scramble). The video emphasizes waste reduction and bulk buying, plus storage tips like freezing produce to extend shelf life.

video-vegan-recipes-goodful-1hwyiwi6yok-.title: Store-Bought vs Local Vegan Mac 'N' Cheese: Three-Way Tasting and a Homemade Sauce
video-vegan-recipes-goodful-1hwyiwi6yok-.summary: This Goodful video presents a friendly comparison of three vegan mac and cheese options: two store-bought boxed products and a homemade version made with mostly locally sourced ingredients. Host Merle announces a store-bought versus locally sourced vegan mac and cheese challenge, then demonstrates how to prepare a homemade sauce by boiling carrot, potato, and onion, saving some cooking water, and blending the vegetables into a creamy sauce. Throughout the tasting, the host shares personality-driven commentary and environmental rationale for choosing plant-based meals, noting that vegan choices can reduce greenhouse gas emissions and food waste. The segment culminates in a taste test where the local-market mac is highlighted for its ingredients and flavor, while remarks acknowledge that plant-based does not always equal traditional cheese in texture. The video blends practical cooking steps with environmental messaging and light humor to encourage viewers to incorporate vegan meals into their routines.

video-vegan-recipes-goodful-28bsngnt2m8-.title: Five-Dollar vs $35 Vegan Pizza: Budget Showdown
